questions.question: Postgres vs MySQL vs Aurora vs CockroachDB — how do you pick a relational DB in 2026?
questions.title: Postgres vs MySQL vs Aurora vs CockroachDB
questions.direct_answer: **Postgres** is the 2026 default: richest feature set (JSONB, full-text, geospatial, pgvector, CTEs, window functions, logical replication), strongest type system, and remarkable scaling up to 10–10TB+ on a single node. **MySQL** (especially 8.0+) still leads in raw simple-query throughput and is the Rails/PHP lingua franca, but has weaker JSON, no CTE window-function parity, and a fragmented ecosystem (Oracle MySQL vs MariaDB). **Aurora (Postgres/MySQL-compatible)** is AWS's rewrite: 3× throughput, shared storage, 128TB, fast failover — pay AWS premium to offload operations. **CockroachDB / Spanner / YugabyteDB** are distributed SQL: horizontal scale + ACID + global — choose when you've outgrown a single Postgres node and need strong consistency, accepting cross-region latency cost. Practical rule: **start with managed Postgres (RDS or Aurora Postgres); move to CockroachDB only when you have real global/horizontal scale needs.**

interviewer_intent.testing: Pragmatic relational DB selection; understanding managed vs self-hosted and distributed SQL
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Reaching for NoSQL when Postgres would scale fine; ignoring Aurora cost; over-engineering with Spanner early
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Discuss Postgres extensions (pgvector, Citus, TimescaleDB), Aurora I/O-optimized, MySQL group replication vs Galera, CockroachDB serial vs region-aware schema

sections.title: The Relational DB Landscape in 2026
sections.content:
The relational world looks very different from ten years ago. Five practical options cover 95% of choices:

**1. Postgres** — the pragmatic default.
- Rich SQL (CTEs, window functions, `FILTER`), JSONB with indexable operators, full-text search (tsvector + GIN), geospatial (PostGIS), pub/sub (LISTEN/NOTIFY), logical replication, powerful extensions (pgvector for AI, TimescaleDB for time-series, Citus for distribution, pg_cron for scheduling).
- Mature ecosystem; MIT-style license; no corporate capture.

**2. MySQL** (Oracle) / **MariaDB** (community fork) — still massive in Rails, PHP, WordPress, and older enterprise.
- MySQL 8.0+ has closed many gaps (CTEs, window functions, roles).
- Simpler storage engine (InnoDB is default) with strong row-locking.
- Preferred when team expertise or legacy dictates.
- MariaDB diverged; features differ; pick one stack.

**3. Aurora** (AWS, Postgres- or MySQL-compatible) — same SQL as Postgres/MySQL, but AWS rewrote the storage layer.
- Shared 128TB storage; 6-way replication across 3 AZs; fast failover; read replicas without IO cost.
- Premium price, but removes much ops work.
- Aurora Serverless v2 autoscales compute.
- **Aurora I/O-Optimized** plan (no per-IO charges) is excellent for write-heavy workloads.

**4. CockroachDB / Google Spanner / YugabyteDB / TiDB** — distributed SQL (NewSQL).
- SQL + ACID + horizontal scale + multi-region.
- Spanner pioneered (Google internal); CockroachDB brought it to open source. YugabyteDB uses Postgres wire protocol.
- TiDB is MySQL-compatible with TiKV storage layer.
- Pay the latency cost of cross-region consensus (Paxos/Raft).
- Use when one-region Postgres/MySQL won't scale or when you need global strong consistency.

**5. Cloud-specific managed** — RDS/CloudSQL/AlloyDB (Google), Azure Database, Planetscale (MySQL with Vitess). Planetscale notable for branching-style schema changes and global scale.

**What you don't usually pick anymore:**
- **Oracle / SQL Server** — large enterprise lock-in only; licensing painful
- **SQLite** — great for embedded (mobile, CLI); new players (Turso, LiteFS) add replication but not OLTP default
- **Self-hosted Postgres on EC2 without Patroni/PgBouncer/backups setup** — unless you have strong DBA expertise

sections.title: Side-by-Side
sections.content:
| Aspect | Postgres | MySQL | Aurora (PG/MySQL) | CockroachDB |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **SQL depth** | Best: CTE, window, JSON ops, rich types | Good 8.0+; historically weaker | Same as source | Postgres-compatible subset |
| **JSON support** | JSONB with indexable ops | JSON (text-like) | Same as source | JSONB-compatible |
| **Full-text** | Built-in tsvector + GIN | Built-in (less rich) | Same as source | Limited |
| **Geospatial** | PostGIS (gold standard) | Basic | Same as source | Limited |
| **Vector / AI** | pgvector extension | (none native) | Aurora Postgres pgvector | (none native) |
| **Partitioning** | Declarative; mature | Supported | Same as source | Native ranges |
| **Sharding** | Citus extension; manual | Vitess, custom | No built-in | Native (automatic) |
| **Max single-node data** | 10–100TB realistic | Similar | 128TB managed | Unlimited (horizontal) |
| **Replication** | Logical + physical | Row-based binlog, Group Replication | Shared storage | Raft per range |
| **Failover** | Patroni / managed ~30–60s | Similar | <30s managed | Automatic, region-aware |
| **Multi-region** | Possible with logical + app logic | Harder | Aurora Global DB | Native, 1st-class |
| **Consistency** | Strong (single node), eventual replica | Strong primary, eventual replica | Strong (primary) | Strong (serializable) |
| **ACID across shards** | No | No | No | Yes |
| **Latency** | Sub-ms local | Sub-ms local | Sub-ms local | Cross-region consensus adds 50–200ms |
| **Cost** | $ self-host / $$ managed | $ / $$ | $$$–$$$$ premium | $$$$ at scale |
| **Best fit** | Default OLTP; 90% of apps | Rails/PHP/legacy | AWS-heavy with scale + ops offload | Global SaaS, strong consistency required |

sections.title: Decision Framework
sections.content:
**Step 1: Managed or self-hosted?**

- **Managed** (RDS, Aurora, CloudSQL, Azure DB): default unless you have strong DBA expertise or specific requirement. Saves weeks of ops.
- **Self-hosted** (Postgres on VMs/K8s, Patroni, PgBouncer): full control, lower cost at scale (> 100+ nodes), requires DBA team.

**Step 2: Pick the engine family.**

- **Postgres** — default. Richer SQL, extensions, modern features.
- **MySQL** — if team expertise, Rails/PHP stack, or integrating with MySQL-first tools (Vitess, Planetscale).
- **Oracle / SQL Server** — only when existing corporate contract or specific feature requires.

**Step 3: Pick the topology.**

- **Single primary + read replicas**: default for OLTP under ~10TB and < 50K writes/sec. Vertical scaling + read replicas goes far.
- **Aurora**: AWS-native with more headroom; trade cost for ops simplicity and better replica performance.
- **Citus / Vitess**: shard on top of Postgres/MySQL; keeps engine, adds horizontal.
- **CockroachDB / Spanner / YugabyteDB**: when single-node can't scale writes, or when you need multi-region ACID.

**Step 4: Address specific requirements.**

- **Time-series**: Postgres + TimescaleDB extension (or InfluxDB / ClickHouse as separate system)
- **Full-text search**: Postgres tsvector OR Elasticsearch alongside
- **Geospatial**: Postgres + PostGIS (no real competition)
- **Vector / RAG**: Postgres + pgvector (moderate scale) or Pinecone/Weaviate (large)
- **Analytical load**: separate DW (Snowflake, BigQuery, ClickHouse) + ETL/CDC
- **JSON-heavy**: Postgres JSONB usually enough; true document-centric → MongoDB
- **Global multi-region writes**: CockroachDB / Spanner / Aurora Global DB

**Step 5: Cost model the choice.**

- Postgres on EC2: cheap compute, your ops cost high
- RDS Postgres: moderate cost, minimal ops
- Aurora Postgres: premium compute + storage; savings on replicas and ops
- CockroachDB serverless: pay per request; expensive at high throughput vs Aurora
- CockroachDB self-hosted: cheap compute, complex ops

**Common team patterns by company stage:**

| Stage | Typical Pick |
|---|---|
| Startup MVP | Managed Postgres (RDS/Supabase/Neon) |
| Series A–B | RDS/Aurora Postgres + Redis + S3 |
| Series C+ scale | Aurora Postgres + read replicas + CDC to Snowflake |
| Multi-region SaaS | CockroachDB or Spanner or Aurora Global DB |
| Massive horizontal | Cassandra/Scylla (wide-column), DynamoDB, or CockroachDB |

**Specific 'when to pick what' cues:**

- 'My Postgres is maxing out writes at 10K/sec on a db.r6.8xlarge.' → Move to Aurora (more headroom) or shard (Citus) or migrate to distributed SQL.
- 'I need strict cross-region consistency.' → CockroachDB / Spanner (Aurora Global DB is async).
- 'I need search-as-you-type.' → Elasticsearch alongside Postgres.
- 'I need ACID across services.' → Saga + outbox (pattern). Not distributed transactions.
- 'I want to save cost on I/O-heavy workload.' → Aurora I/O-Optimized plan.
- 'I need zero-downtime schema changes at scale.' → Planetscale (MySQL) or Aurora with gh-ost/pg_squeeze.
- 'I have billions of time-series rows.' → TimescaleDB extension on Postgres, or ClickHouse.

sections.title: Trade-offs and Hard Truths
sections.content:
**Postgres scales further than most people think.** Single r6i.16xlarge or db.r6.16xlarge can handle 10–100K writes/sec and tens of TB. Before assuming you need distributed SQL, run the numbers.

**MySQL 8.0 closed many gaps.** CTEs, window functions, check constraints, roles, descending indexes. But JSON is weaker, collation/character set history is messy (utf8 vs utf8mb4), and ecosystem is bifurcated (Oracle MySQL vs MariaDB vs Percona).

**Aurora is not Postgres.** It's a Postgres-compatible wire protocol with rewritten storage. Some extensions aren't supported; performance characteristics differ; certain queries slower (some faster). Test your workload before committing.

**Aurora cost surprises.** Per-I/O charges (before I/O-Optimized) can balloon for write-heavy workloads. Storage also charges for unused capacity after large DELETEs (retain until VACUUM FULL). I/O-Optimized plan mitigates at higher compute cost.

**Distributed SQL latency.** CockroachDB / Spanner cross-region writes cost ~50–200ms for consensus. Per-row writes in multi-region mode are substantially slower than single-region Postgres. Design schema (regional vs global tables) to localize most writes.

**Joins across shards.** Distributed SQL handles them, but performance varies. Schema design matters: co-locate related rows via region pinning or interleaving.

**ACID across shards works but isn't free.** CockroachDB achieves serializable isolation via 2PC under the hood. Contention on hot rows causes retries visible to app (`40001 serialization_failure` in Postgres mode).

**Connection pooling matters everywhere.**
- Postgres default 100 connections; actual apps need PgBouncer or similar
- Aurora has higher limits but still benefits from pooling (RDS Proxy)
- CockroachDB has different pooling characteristics; uses its own proxy

**Operational tooling gaps.**
- Postgres: `pg_dump`, `pg_basebackup`, Patroni, WAL-G, pgBackRest, Barman, pgBouncer, PgCat
- MySQL: `mysqldump`, Percona XtraBackup, ProxySQL, Vitess
- Aurora: AWS manages most; less flexibility
- CockroachDB: built-in; less third-party

**Migration path matters.**
- Postgres → Aurora Postgres: easy (same protocol)
- MySQL → Aurora MySQL: easy
- Postgres → CockroachDB: mostly compatible; test carefully (some Postgres features absent or semantics differ)
- Aurora → Postgres: possible but operationally complex

**Backup and PITR.**
- Managed offerings include PITR automatically; test restores quarterly
- Self-hosted needs deliberate setup (WAL archiving, pgBackRest, etc.)
- Verify backup actually works; 'I have backups' is untested until you restore

**Replication lag.** Async replicas lag. Read-your-write consistency issues. Options: read from primary after writes, session-based routing, synchronous replication (slower), or read-after-write tokens.

**Hot partition / hot row problem.** Every DB has it. Monotonic primary keys cause single-node hotspots; use ULIDs, UUIDs, or sharding keys. CockroachDB has auto-split for ranges.

**Schema migrations at scale.**
- Adding indexes online: `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` in Postgres; `ALGORITHM=INPLACE` in MySQL 8
- Large ALTER TABLE: use pg_squeeze, gh-ost, pt-online-schema-change
- Planetscale (MySQL): branching model for schema changes
- CockroachDB: schema changes online via background jobs

**Licensing and open-source concerns.**
- Postgres: PostgreSQL License (MIT-style), no corporate capture
- MySQL (Oracle): GPL + commercial; Oracle's stewardship debated
- MariaDB: fork; different features; BSL for some enterprise features
- CockroachDB: BSL (Business Source License); eventually Apache
- Aurora: AWS-proprietary compute + storage

**Observability:**
- `pg_stat_statements` for query performance (Postgres)
- Performance Schema / sys schema (MySQL)
- Aurora Performance Insights (GUI)
- CockroachDB DB Console + SQL observability
- Always monitor: slow queries, lock contention, replication lag, connection saturation, disk growth, IO latency

**Developer ergonomics.**
- Postgres: best SQL feel, best error messages, best psql
- MySQL: very fast for simple queries; CLI less rich
- Aurora: basically same as source DB
- CockroachDB: Postgres wire protocol but different error codes; operational patterns differ

**The strategic defaults in 2026:**
- **Managed Postgres** (RDS Postgres or Aurora Postgres) for 80% of applications
- **Aurora Postgres** when AWS-heavy and scale/ops matter
- **Supabase / Neon / Turso** for startup speed
- **MySQL / Aurora MySQL** when team expertise dictates
- **CockroachDB / Spanner** when you genuinely need distributed SQL; not as premature optimization

sections.title: Key Points
sections.content:
- **Managed Postgres** (RDS or Aurora) is the 2026 default for OLTP
- **Postgres scales further than people think** — tens of TB and 10K+ writes/sec on single node
- **Aurora** trades premium cost for 128TB, fast failover, better replica performance
- **MySQL 8.0+** closed many gaps but JSON and ecosystem bifurcation remain concerns
- **CockroachDB / Spanner** only when you need horizontal + global + ACID; accept cross-region latency
- **Extensions make Postgres remarkable**: pgvector, PostGIS, TimescaleDB, Citus
- **Aurora I/O-Optimized** plan prevents I/O-charge surprises for write-heavy workloads
- **Replication lag is real** — design read-after-write carefully
- **Connection pooling** (PgBouncer, RDS Proxy) is mandatory at scale
- **Test restores quarterly** — untested backups are theoretical

sections.content:
Postgres is the 2026 default. Five practical options cover 95% of choices.

**Postgres**

**Aurora (AWS, Postgres- or MySQL-compatible)**

- 128TB shared storage; 6-way replication across 3 AZs; fast failover
- Read replicas without IO cost
- Premium price but removes ops work
- Aurora I/O-Optimized plan excellent for write-heavy
- Aurora Serverless v2 autoscales compute

**Distributed SQL: CockroachDB, Spanner, YugabyteDB, TiDB**
- SQL plus ACID plus horizontal scale plus multi-region
- Spanner pioneered; CockroachDB brought it open source
- YugabyteDB uses Postgres wire protocol
- TiDB MySQL-compatible with TiKV storage
- Pay latency cost of cross-region consensus (Paxos/Raft)
- Use when one-region Postgres/MySQL won't scale or global strong consistency needed

**Cloud-specific managed**
- CloudSQL, AlloyDB (Google), Azure Database
- Planetscale (MySQL with Vitess); branching-style schema changes
- Supabase, Neon, Turso for startup speed

**Decision framework**

*Step 1: Managed or self-hosted*
- Managed is default unless strong DBA expertise or specific requirement
- Self-hosted: full control, lower cost at scale

*Step 2: Engine family*
- Postgres default; MySQL if team expertise or Rails/PHP
- Oracle/SQL Server only for existing contracts

*Step 3: Topology*
- Single primary + read replicas for OLTP under 10TB and 50K writes/sec
- Aurora for more headroom; pay for ops simplicity
- Citus or Vitess for sharding existing engines
- CockroachDB or Spanner when single-node can't scale or need multi-region ACID

*Step 4: Specific requirements*
- Time-series: Postgres + TimescaleDB, or ClickHouse
- Full-text: Postgres tsvector, or Elasticsearch alongside
- Geospatial: Postgres + PostGIS
- Vector/RAG: pgvector (moderate), Pinecone (large scale)
- Analytical: separate warehouse (Snowflake, BigQuery) + CDC

**Practical rule: start with managed Postgres; move to CockroachDB only when real global or horizontal scale needs**

**Trade-offs and hard truths**

*Postgres scales further than most think*
- r6i.16xlarge or db.r6.16xlarge handles 10 to 100K writes/sec and tens of TB
- Run numbers before assuming distributed SQL

*MySQL 8.0 closed many gaps*
- But JSON weaker, ecosystem bifurcated

*Aurora is not Postgres*
- Postgres-compatible wire protocol with rewritten storage
- Some extensions not supported; test workload

*Aurora cost surprises*
- Per-I/O charges balloon for write-heavy
- Storage charges for unused capacity after DELETEs until VACUUM FULL
- I/O-Optimized plan mitigates at higher compute cost

*Distributed SQL latency*
- Cross-region writes cost 50 to 200ms for consensus
- Design schema (regional vs global tables) to localize writes

*ACID across shards isn't free*
- 2PC under the hood; contention causes retries
- serialization_failure visible to app

*Connection pooling matters everywhere*
- PgBouncer, RDS Proxy, built-in CockroachDB proxy

*Replication lag is real*
- Async replicas lag
- Read-after-write issues; plan session routing or sync replication

*Hot partition problem*
- Monotonic primary keys cause single-node hotspots
- Use ULIDs, UUIDs, sharding keys

*Schema migrations at scale*
- CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY (Postgres)
- ALGORITHM=INPLACE (MySQL 8)
- gh-ost, pt-online-schema-change for large ALTERs
- Planetscale branching model; CockroachDB online schema changes

*Backup and PITR*
- Managed includes PITR; test restores quarterly
- Untested backups are theoretical

**Team patterns by stage**
- Startup MVP: managed Postgres (RDS, Supabase, Neon)
- Series A-B: RDS/Aurora Postgres + Redis + S3
- Series C+: Aurora Postgres + read replicas + CDC to Snowflake
- Multi-region SaaS: CockroachDB, Spanner, or Aurora Global DB
- Massive horizontal: Cassandra/Scylla, DynamoDB, or CockroachDB

**When to pick what**
- Maxing writes on single Postgres: Aurora, shard via Citus, or migrate to distributed SQL
- Strict cross-region consistency: CockroachDB or Spanner (Aurora Global DB is async)
- Search-as-you-type: Elasticsearch alongside
- ACID across services: saga plus outbox; not distributed transactions
- I/O-heavy cost savings: Aurora I/O-Optimized
- Zero-downtime schema at scale: Planetscale or gh-ost/pg_squeeze

**Observability**
- pg_stat_statements (Postgres)
- Performance Schema / sys (MySQL)
- Aurora Performance Insights
- CockroachDB DB Console
- Monitor: slow queries, lock contention, replication lag, connection saturation, disk, IO latency

**The strategic answer**
- Managed Postgres is default for 80% of applications
- Aurora when AWS-heavy and scale/ops matter
- CockroachDB or Spanner only when genuinely needed
- Test backups quarterly; connection pool always; plan replication lag
- Don't reach for NoSQL when Postgres would scale fine
- Licensing and ecosystem matter; Postgres has cleanest governance
